title: Batch/cmd launcher prints non-ASCII UI (box-drawing/emoji) without a chcp 65001 codepage switch
description: Windows .bat/.cmd launchers authored in a UTF-8 editor frequently embed box-drawing characters (U+2500 family: ─ ═ ║ ╔ ╗ ╚ ╝), check-marks (U+2713), arrows, or emoji inside echo banners and menus. cmd.exe renders a batch file under the console's active OEM codepage (commonly 437/850), so those UTF-8 bytes display as mojibake (e.g. â•”â•â•) — the menu still runs but looks corrupted and option text can become unreadable. The canonical fix is to switch the console to UTF-8 with `chcp 65001 >nul` before the first echo. Detected while validating every Start script and launcher batch: Launch-CFRMenu.bat, Launch-GUI.bat and tests\Test-LaunchGUI-Switches.bat each printed box-drawing banners with no chcp directive.
detection_method: Binary/text scan (batch/cmd only). Decode the file as UTF-8, then scan each line that is NOT a REM/:: comment for any character > U+007F. If such a displayed (echo/set/prompt) line exists AND the file contains no `chcp 65001` directive anywhere, flag line 1 occurrence. Comment-only Unicode (REM ── headers, em-dashes in REM) is ignored because comments are never rendered, keeping the pattern false-positive-free.
scan_logic: UTF-8 decode bytes; if no /^\s*chcp\s+65001\b/im match, walk non-comment lines; first line containing a char > 0x7F => finding (line number reported).
false_positive_note: Lines beginning with REM, @REM or :: are skipped — box-drawing/em-dash inside comments (e.g. 'REM ── Bootstrap') is cosmetic-only and never displayed, so it is intentionally NOT flagged. A file that uses Unicode purely in comments needs no chcp and produces zero findings. Only displayed text (echo/set/prompt lines) triggers the SIN. Requiring `chcp 65001` specifically (not just any chcp) is deliberate: switching to 850/437 would not render UTF-8 box-drawing correctly.
preventionRule: Any .bat/.cmd that echoes non-ASCII UI (box-drawing, check-marks, emoji) MUST issue `chcp 65001 >nul` before the first such echo, OR restrict displayed UI to plain ASCII. Prefer chcp for files whose source is UTF-8; prefer ASCII art for maximum portability.
remedy:
REM BEFORE (mojibake under OEM codepage)
@echo off
echo ╔═══ MENU ═══╗
REM AFTER (renders correctly)
@echo off
chcp 65001 >nul
echo ╔═══ MENU ═══╗
